name: Simo decoction
short: Reported reactions: rash, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhoea. Main ingredient areca seed has potential cancer-causing effects; a 2024 review found no reports of cancer or severe reactions.
text: A 2024 review describes Simo decoction as a Chinese patent medicine sold as an oral solution, whose main ingredient is areca seed (Areca catechu), known for potential carcinogenic (cancer-causing) effects. That review of post-marketing research, the literature and adverse-reaction databases found that common adverse drug reactions include skin rash, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhoea; it found no studies reporting severe reactions such as cancer, and no reports of toxicity from areca seed in the WHO and Chinese adverse-reaction databases. In a randomized trial in 224 critically ill adults, in which Simo decoction or domperidone suspension was given for 24 hours to help place a nasoenteric tube past the stomach outlet, the incidence of any adverse events and deaths in intensive care did not differ between the groups; the abstract gives no numbers. In a placebo-controlled trial in 138 people with early liver dysfunction after liver transplantation, the decoction showed no adverse effects on recovery of liver or kidney function; the abstract says adverse events and use alongside tacrolimus (an immunosuppressant) were analysed but does not report those results. No other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
